title: Solidity analyzer surface over the pinned real corpus
perfIsQualifiedRule: loadAvg1 < 8. A perFileMs taken above that is contention, not a lane budget — measured on a sibling lane whose artifact published 228 → 246 → 91 ms/file across three runs of an UNCHANGED analyzer. /proc/pressure/memory is recorded too, because load is the wrong signal when the box is memory-stalled: PSI, not loadavg, is what stalls.

totals.notExercisedNote: `imports` is expected here and is NOT a gap: imports are modelled as `references` edges carrying `metadata.import: true`, the settled convention for this repo (PowerShell PS-7 for the same reason). The count of those edges is `tiers.import_based`, and every one of them is checked by the fixtures' `expectImports`.

callCalleeKinds._note: SOL-15. Every `calls` edge carries a `calleeKind`, so the `unresolvedCallTargets` count below no longer mixes four unrelated things. `conversion` and `namespaceBuiltin` name a primitive type word or a member of `abi`/`type`/`super`/`this` — provably not project symbols, and excluded from it. `localFunction`/`inheritedMember`/`libraryFunction`/`modifierInvocation` resolve against THIS FILE's declarations and the inheritance closure. `external` is the real residue: a member or free function declared in another file, which a per-file analyzer cannot see — measured at 0 for localFunction and inheritedMember over the whole corpus, because OpenZeppelin is modularised so thoroughly that almost every call leaves the file.

byCalleeKind._note: The point of SOL-15: the unresolved count is no longer one undifferentiated class. `errorRevert` dominates because SOL-15 REPAIRED the `revert_statement` case, which had never fired for any input — so these 453 custom-error call edges did not exist in this lane at all before, and the unresolved count ROSE when the lane got more correct. `external` is the genuine residue: a member or free function declared in another file.

analyzerDecisions.natspecNote: SOL-16. `commentsRead` is every `comment` node in the corpus; `commentsAttached` is how many of them landed on a declaration, which is the count that matters because Solidity attaches documentation to what FOLLOWS it. The gap between the two is real: a comment before an expression, or a trailing remark at the end of a body, documents nothing. `documentedSymbols` is the share of the 5,976 symbols that carry a `docstring`, which the store persists to `brain_symbol.docstring` — a column NULL for every Solidity symbol before this.
analyzerDecisions.externalBaseNote: `overridesEmittedExternal` are rows whose base is named by an explicit `override(...)` list but declared in ANOTHER file. The Solidity compiler rejects `override(X)` unless `X` declares the member, so the edge is true for any compiling source; it is carried at 0.75 with `meta.reasonCode: "named-by-override-specifier"` rather than 0.9, because the member's presence is read off the language invariant instead of a declaration. Every one of those targets resolves to a real project symbol (`unknownTargets` is judged project-wide for `overrides`), so the corpus agrees with the edge.

method: Candidates are the corpus's production (non-test) tracked .sol files, drawn by a hash of `repo/relative-path` so the sample is unbiased and reproducible; the digest is recorded so a re-run that drew a DIFFERENT set says so instead of being compared. Every file goes through the production `parseFile`. `damage` is measured with a separate parser and is the GRAMMAR's number, independent of any analyzer decision. `lineNumber` counts relationships carrying a positive line — the analyzer REFUSES a non-positive line at its single emit helper, so this ratio is a completeness check on the emit path, not a quality score. `tiers` is read from the analyzer's own central `evidenceClassFor`, not recomputed here, so it cannot drift from the emit path. `unknownTargets` counts ONLY the kinds whose both ends are locally declared by definition — contains, overrides, extends, implements, exports. `calls`, `uses`, `instantiates` and `references` are excluded because their targets may be external, a Yul function, a language-supplied type, or an EVM member. `dupKeys` counts (file, owner, name, kind) tuples emitted more than once; the owner IS part of the key, because a local declared in two functions is two correct declarations. `reservedTargets` uses the lane's own imported predicate (src/ast/solidity-reserved-tokens.ts) — one copy of the rule, because a sibling lane's two instruments each held their own and silently disagreed.
limits: This is NOT a truth oracle. It measures what the analyzer emits and how it changed; whether each edge is CORRECT is F5's question. Everything here can be green with every edge wrong.
`unknownTargets` is a proxy for resolvability, not for correctness: a target that names a real contract which happens to share a spelling with a local symbol counts as resolved.

`unresolvedCallTargets` is NOT expected to be 0 and must not be gated as if it were. `abi.encode(1)` and `payable(a).transfer(1)` are real calls whose targets are EVM/ABI members; Solidity has no syntax that distinguishes them from a user-defined member access, so suppressing them would lose real edges. The top-target list is the adjudication surface.

`storeRefusedDeclarations` counts declarations this lane declined to make because pool-worker.ts's UNIVERSAL denylist would drop the symbol while the analyzer's `contains` edge survived — 2 over the draw (`self` at CrosschainLinked.sol:59, `root` at MerkleTreeMock.sol:15). Both are real Solidity identifiers, so the store's list is over-broad for this language; the fix belongs in pool-worker.ts, which this lane does not own, so the drift between the two lists is checked by script/m60/solidity-reserved-words.ts instead. The refusals are COUNTED so an uncounted one is distinguishable from the analyzer being wrong.

`implementsCrossFileUnresolved` counts `extends` edges that may really be `implements` because the interface is declared in another file. A per-file analyzer cannot see it; the count is reported rather than hidden, and it is a wrong KIND, not a missing edge.

Parse damage is the vendored grammar's, and it is 0 on all 389 production files — so this draw cannot exercise the recovery-region refusal (SOL-6). The fixture `recovery-regions-sol6` forces an ERROR on purpose, because a green 0-damage corpus would otherwise leave that rule untested.
